items.stem: Several teams on one product each finish their own work but only integrate at the very end, causing failures. Nexus addresses this by emphasising:

options.text: Continuous integration and managing cross-team dependencies throughout the Sprint
options.rationale: Correct: Nexus focuses on integration and dependency management to produce one Increment.

options.text: Each team shipping separately with no integration
options.rationale: Separate shipping is exactly the problem.
Nexus reduces, not adds, integration friction.

items.explanation: Correct: Nexus focuses on integration and dependency management to produce one Increment.

items.stem: The Nexus Integration Team exists primarily to:

options.text: Coordinate and coach teams so they produce one integrated Increment
options.rationale: Correct: the NIT focuses on integration across teams.

options.text: Do all the coding for every team
options.rationale: The NIT coordinates; it does not do all the work.
The NIT does not replace the Product Owner.

items.stem: Which TWO practices most reduce cross-team integration problems at scale? (Select TWO)

options.text: Identifying and sequencing dependencies during cross-team refinement
options.rationale: Correct: surfacing dependencies early prevents late collisions.

options.text: Integrating work frequently rather than at the end
options.rationale: Correct: frequent integration avoids a release crunch.

options.text: Letting each team define its own private Definition of Done
Deferring integration testing to after release
options.rationale: Late testing finds failures too late.

items.explanation: Correct: surfacing dependencies early prevents late collisions. Correct: frequent integration avoids a release crunch.
